summary: Remote-controlled shell, filesystem, and self-upgrade agent driven by WebSocket server
details: The package runs a long-lived agent that connects out to a configured WebSocket server and dispatches server-sent messages into privileged local operations on the installer's host. connection/message-router.js routes `terminal_create`/`terminal_input`/`terminal_resize`/`terminal_close` frames into a node-pty child spawning the OS default shell (bash/PowerShell/cmd); bytes received on the socket are written directly to the PTY and PTY output is streamed back, yielding full interactive-shell RCE controlled by whichever server the agent points at. The same dispatcher exposes `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, `transfer_files`, `git_add`/`commit`/`push`, `restart_agent`, and `upgrade_agent` handlers, so the remote party can arbitrarily read/modify/exfiltrate files in workDir and push using the installer's git credentials. connection/upgrade.js handles `upgrade_agent` by generating an `upgrade.sh` that runs `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restarts the systemd/launchd/PM2-managed service, giving the remote server a persistent self-reinstall channel. service/linux.js additionally installs the agent as a system service and mutates PATH (`~/.local/bin`, `~/.npm-global/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin`) as part of that persistence. No per-command user consent is required for any of these operations once the agent is running.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
